workspace.estimateNoEntryNote: Leave No Entry at 0. It is the unsized state, and a non-zero value would give an unsized item a forecast it was never given.

integrations.title: Source control
integrations.subtitle: Connect GitHub once — repositories are discovered automatically and their pull requests & commits link to work items by key (e.g. US-42).

orgs.title: Connected organizations
orgs.disconnectMessage: Rova stops receiving events from this installation and its discovered repositories are deactivated. Existing links on work items are kept. You can reconnect at any time.

empty.title: No GitHub organization connected
empty.description: Install the Rova GitHub App on your organization, then connect it here — every repository it can access appears automatically and starts syncing.

connectDialog.title: Connect a GitHub organization
connectDialog.description: Pick an installation of the Rova GitHub App. Its repositories are discovered automatically and back-filled.
connectDialog.empty: No available installations. Install the Rova GitHub App on your organization first, then reopen this dialog.

empty.title: No repositories yet
empty.description: Connect a GitHub organization above, or add a repository manually below.

integrations.removeMessage: This stops linking new pull requests & commits from this repository. Existing links on work items are kept.
integrations.sync: Sync now — backfill existing PRs & commits

webhook.title: Manual webhook setup
webhook.description: Only needed for repositories outside a connected GitHub App installation. Add this webhook to the repository (content type application/json, events: Pull requests + Pushes) using your SCM webhook secret.

manualAdd.title: Add a repository manually
manualAdd.description: For repositories not covered by a connected installation. Matched to this workspace by owner/name.

tabDescriptions.profile: Your personal account details and preferences.
tabDescriptions.notifications: Choose how you're notified for each kind of event.
tabDescriptions.workspace: Workspace name, regional defaults, and details.
tabDescriptions.members: Manage who can access this workspace, their role and status.
tabDescriptions.teams: Organize people into teams, assign leads and projects.
tabDescriptions.audit: Review recent activity and changes across the workspace.
tabDescriptions.integrations: Connect GitHub and manage repository sync.
tabDescriptions.apiTokens: Credentials a machine uses on your behalf. Each one carries your permissions and nothing more.
tabDescriptions.archive: Archived projects and teams — restore one, or delete it for good.

empty.title: No API tokens
empty.description: Create one to let a script, a CI job or an integration call Rova as you.

apiTokens.revokeMessage: Anything using this token stops working on its next request. This cannot be undone — a replacement is a new token.
apiTokens.footnote: A token inherits your permissions at the moment of every request, so access you lose is access it loses. Send it as a bearer token: Authorization: Bearer rly_…

create.title: New API token
create.subtitle: It will be shown once, immediately after it is created.
create.nameHint: What will use it. This is how you will recognise it when deciding what to revoke.
create.expiryHint: Every token expires. {{max}} days is the maximum the API accepts.
create.scopeNote: The token inherits your permissions. It can never do more than you can, and it stops being able to do what you stop being able to do.

created.title: Token created
created.warning: Copy it now. Rova stores only a hash, so this is the one and only time it can be shown — a lost token is revoked and replaced, not recovered.
created.label: Token for {{name}}
created.usage: Send it as a bearer token: Authorization: Bearer <token>

archive.emptyDescription: Archived projects and teams collect here, where they can be restored or deleted. Archive one from Workspaces & Projects.
archive.footnote: Deleting is permanent. A team can only be deleted while it holds no delivery history; the server refuses and explains itself when it does.

project.restoreMessage: Restore {{name}}? It becomes an active project again and reappears in every project picker.
project.deleteMessage: This removes {{name}} and everything filed under it — work items, iterations, releases and reports. It cannot be undone.

team.restoreMessage: Restore {{name}}? It becomes available for new membership and reappears in every team picker.
team.deleteMessage: Delete {{name}}? This is allowed only while the team holds no delivery history. Nothing is removed if it still does.
